Affordability 6: $2,100/mo read on the listing brokerage's own page - inside the $2,200 cap but exactly at the $2,100 comfortable ceiling, so no headroom for the tenant-paid gas heat. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $2,100 is $75,600/yr, above the $71k top of the band, so income documentation is a live risk. Eligibility 8: market-rate, no age rule and no AMI limit; screening is the normal credit-plus-references kind, with a $50/applicant fee. Accessibility 9: 'First floor' is stated on the brokerage page I read and on the Apartments.com row the controller rendered - two independent statements of the profile's hard filter. Suitability 10: two off-street spaces stated (base 8), +1 for 793 sq ft over the 700 floor, +1 in-unit washer/dryer, +1 for 2BR giving the project room; capped at 10. The one gap is storage - 'custom storage' in a bathroom is not a basement. Location 9: Plymouth, a preferred town, walking distance to the downtown waterfront and about 5 minutes to Route 3. Actionability 9: ACTIVE on 2026-09-10 with a stated 2026-10-08 date, inside the December 2026 window. Lifestyle 9: 3 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - harbor, Nelson Park and the bike path; walkable downtown center; quiet residential side street).

Red flags

A SEPARATE listing at the same street address - 11 Peck Ave UNIT 2, MLS 73344451, second floor, also 2BR at $2,100 - is marked RENTED. Same building, same landlord, same photos and near-identical copy. Do not let an agent or an aggregator substitute Unit 2 for Unit 1: the first floor is the whole point of this lead.

Advantages

The only lead in this slice that clears every stated need at once: first floor, TWO off-street spaces, in-unit washer/dryer, 793 sq ft (over the 700 floor), 2BR, $2,100 (at but not over the comfortable ceiling), and an Oct 8 2026 date inside the December window. Confirmed ACTIVE on the listing brokerage's own page on 2026-09-10.

Drawbacks

$2,100 is exactly the comfortable ceiling with no headroom; no dishwasher named; no pets; a 3x-annual-rent income test ($75,600) sits above the top of the household's income band; no basement/garage/shed for project storage.

Affordability 7: $1,950/mo on the brokerage page, $250 under the cap and $150 under the comfortable ceiling, and the landlord absorbs trash, landscaping and plowing, which is real money on the South Shore. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $1,950 is $70,200/yr, just inside the $71k top of the band but far above its $43k bottom. Eligibility 8: market-rate, no age rule, no AMI limit, no stated screening beyond the ordinary; year-round rather than seasonal, which is what sinks the two furnished leads in this slice. Accessibility 9: a detached single-storey cottage, listing floor level 1 - no stairs anywhere. Suitability 9: two off-street spaces (base 8), -1 for 595 sq ft under the 700 floor, +1 in-unit laundry, +1 for 2BR. The square footage is the honest reservation: the second bedroom will be a small one. Location 9: Plymouth, preferred town, about 10 minutes to Route 3 by estimate. Actionability 9: ACTIVE and available immediately on 2026-09-10, well inside the December 2026 window. Lifestyle 6: 2 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - semi-private beach access comes with the tenancy; quiet detached cottage on a 0.28-acre lot; NO walkable centre - this is a shore neighbourhood, everything is a drive).

Red flags

None found. The contradiction search (WebSearch 2026-09-10) turned up an independent MLS-fed restatement of the same figures ($1,950, 2BR/1BA, 595 sq ft, available immediately) rather than a disagreement.

Advantages

Single-storey, no stairs at all - the cleanest answer in the slice to the first-floor filter. Two off-street spaces, in-unit laundry, 2BR, available now, and the landlord pays trash, landscaping AND plowing, which removes the winter-parking chore that worried the household. $1,950 leaves $150/mo under the comfortable ceiling. Pets allowed.

Drawbacks

595 sq ft is roughly 100 sq ft UNDER the profile's 700 floor, and a 2BR that small leaves almost no project room; no basement, garage or shed is named; no dishwasher mentioned; the phone number came from an aggregator, not the brokerage page.

Red flags

A WebSearch results summary for this MLS number reported rents scattered from $1,900 to $2,900 (figures of $2,200 and $2,600 named) and a size of 1,200 sq ft. None of those figures appears on either brokerage page I actually read, both of which say $1,975 and 730 sq ft. Treat the scattered numbers as aggregator noise, but confirm the rent on the call before anyone signs anything.

Advantages

Confirmed ACTIVE at $1,975 on TWO independent brokerage pages on 2026-09-10 - Compass and the listing brokerage's own Jack Conway Kingston rental index. First floor and single living level with an 'accessible entrance', TWO off-street spaces, in-unit washer/dryer, 730 sq ft over the 700 floor, pets allowed, pond frontage and a private patio, in a preferred town five minutes from Route 3, available now.

Drawbacks

1BR only - no project room, which is the household's stated preference and the reason this does not outrank 11 Peck Ave. No dishwasher named. No storage building. 44 days on market with no price cut is a mild signal the rent is above what the unit is fetching.

Advantages

Reported lot rent ($450-550/mo, unconfirmed) would be well under the $2,200 budget cap even combined with home-ownership costs; single-story manufactured homes solve the first-floor/no-stairs need outright; 55+ age-appropriate; preferred town.

Drawbacks

Requires a separate, unknown home-purchase cost on top of monthly lot rent; not a rental in the conventional sense, so it does not offer the flexibility/no-large-capital-outlay profile a straight rental would.

Affordability 8: $1,900/mo INCLUDING water, sewer and cable television, which is a genuinely lower all-in cost than the number suggests - $300 under the cap. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $1,900 is $68,400/yr, inside the $71k top of the band. Eligibility 8: market-rate, no age rule and no AMI limit; first, last, references and renter's insurance is the ordinary ask. Accessibility 6: second floor of a multi-family, which the profile accepts if it is one short flight - but the flight count is not stated and the building dates from 1785, so the stairs are as likely to be steep and narrow as short. The basement laundry adds a second staircase. Suitability 8: two off-street spaces (base 8), +1 for exactly 700 sq ft at the floor, -1 for 1BR with no project room; no laundry bonus, since the machines are in the cellar. Location 9: Kingston, preferred town, about 4 minutes to Route 3 at Exit 20. Actionability 3: PENDING - under agreement on the listing agent's own page on 2026-09-10, so not rentable now, though a pending rental that falls through is a live lead and the same agent has other Plymouth-area stock. Lifestyle 4: 1 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - the Jones River and Gray's Beach; NOT quiet, Main St is Route 3A; no compact walkable centre). | Timeline: actionability 3 to 2 (band CLOSED)

Red flags

The two MLS-fed brokerage feeds disagree about whether this unit is still on the market. The listing brokerage's own Coldwell Banker page marked it PENDING when I read it on 2026-09-10, while the Jack Conway Kingston rental index still carried '59 Main St UNIT 2S - $1,900' as a live rental listing on the same day. No second AVAILABILITY value is recorded as an observation, because the Conway index publishes a price row rather than a status - its silence is not a claim that the unit is open. The listing agent's own page is the better evidence and the record follows it, but the discrepancy is worth one question on the call.

Advantages

If it comes back on the market it is a strong row: TWO off-street spaces, exactly 700 sq ft, a dishwasher, a deck, central air, and water, sewer and cable included at $1,900 - four minutes from Route 3 in a preferred town. The listing agent, Jill O'Brien, is also the agent on 11 Peck Ave Unit 1, so one call can cover both.

Drawbacks

It is under agreement. Second floor of a building put up in 1785, with the flight count unstated and no possibility of an elevator. 1BR, so no project room. Laundry is in a 1785 basement, which is a set of cellar stairs of its own. No pets.

Affordability 8: $1,800/mo, $400 under the cap and $300 under the comfortable ceiling - the cheapest year-round unfurnished lead outside downtown Plymouth, though the tenant carries all utilities. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $1,800 is $64,800/yr, inside the $71k top of the band. Eligibility 7 rather than the usual 8: market-rate with no age rule and no AMI limit, but the screening is the strictest in the slice - a 650+ credit score and TWO MONTHS of income verification, which a Social Security household documents differently from a wage earner and which is a real friction rather than a formality. Accessibility 6: a second-floor apartment with the flight count unstated and no elevator claimed, so it sits inside the profile's one-short-flight allowance only conditionally; the 'D' building designator hints that ground-floor units may exist in the complex, which is worth asking. Suitability 3: parking is not mentioned anywhere so the base is 5 (unknown), -1 for 600 sq ft under the 700 floor, -1 for 1BR with no project room; the on-site common laundry earns no bonus. Location 6: Marshfield is an adjacent town and this is its eastern shore - about 12 minutes to Route 3, the longest drive in the slice. Actionability 5: ACTIVE and freshly listed on 2026-09-08, but no available date is published anywhere - unknown rather than open, though freshness makes a call likely to be productive. Lifestyle 6: 2 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - the Marshfield beaches and the South River; walkable to shops, restaurants and transit per the broker; NOT quiet on Route 139). Matches the 6 the earlier lifestyle pass gave the other Ocean Street rows at 1520, 1554 and 2093.

Red flags

Parking is not mentioned at all. Every other listing in this slice states parking one way or another, even when the count is missing; total silence on a multi-building complex usually means an unassigned shared lot, which is the arrangement the household most wants to avoid. Second, the screening is the strictest in the slice - 650+ credit and TWO MONTHS of income verification, which a Social Security household answers with benefit award letters rather than pay stubs, and which should be raised with the agent before an application fee is spent.

Advantages

$1,800/mo is $400 under the cap - the cheapest year-round unfurnished lead outside downtown Plymouth - and the listing is the freshest in the slice, updated 2026-09-08. Year-round and unfurnished, hardwood throughout, gas heat, on-site laundry, and near shopping, restaurants and transit on the Marshfield shore.

Drawbacks

Three misses at once: 600 sq ft under the 700 floor, a second floor with the flight count unstated and no elevator claimed, and NO mention of parking anywhere in the listing - for a two-car household that is the deciding gap. Add strict screening (650+ credit, two months of income verification), a 1BR layout, and the longest Route 3 drive in the slice at about 12 minutes.

IMPORTANT AFFORDABILITY FLAG: the 2BR rent ($2,515/mo) exceeds the household's $2,200 market-rate/fixed-affordable cap by $315/mo; only the 1BR ($2,105/mo, undersized for the household's 2BR/project-space preference) fits the budget. | Navigator: Fixed below-market; covered parking + private storage for lease | MINIMUM-INCOME FLOOR applies: 1BR needs ≥$70,950, 2BR needs ≥$84,330 for 2 people; household band $43k–$71k partly clears 1BR; does NOT clear 2BR | Sharp two-tier picture: the affordable program (halsteadplymouth.com/affordable-housing/) is 1BR $2,105 / 2BR $2,515 / 3BR $2,875, with a stated minimum income of $63,150 for the 1BR -- so only the top of the household's $43k-$71k band qualifies, and only the 1BR is anywhere near the $2,100 comfort ceiling. The market units actually available are 1BR+den $2,715-$2,790, 2BR $2,995-$3,190, 3BR $3,625 -- roughly $600-$1,000/mo over the cap. One useful escape hatch printed on the affordable page: 'Applicants who receive a housing subsidy are not subject to the minimum income requirement', which matters once a household member's voucher application resolves. No elevator or floor count is published; unit numbers on the floor-plans page (#10103, #10221, #10303, #1202, #2205, #3310, #4110, #4321) imply at least three levels across several buildings, so accessibility is left unchanged pending the call.

Affordability 6: $2,100/mo is exactly the comfortable ceiling and the tenant pays ALL utilities on top, so the real monthly cost pushes against the $2,200 cap. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $2,100 is $75,600/yr, above the $71k top of the band. Eligibility 8: market-rate, no age rule and no AMI limit; no screening terms published. Accessibility 6: a second-floor walk-up with no elevator - inside the profile's 'one short flight is do-able' allowance only if it IS one short flight, which the listing pointedly does not say. Suitability 4: parking stated but not counted so the base is 5, +1 for 800 sq ft well over the 700 floor, -1 for 1BR with no project room, -1 because no laundry is mentioned in the unit or the building. Location 6: Norwell is an adjacent town on the Route 53 corridor, roughly 7 minutes from Route 3 at Exit 30. Actionability 5: ACTIVE but with no stated available date and about 100 days on market - unknown rather than open, and the long sit is itself a question. Lifestyle 4: 1 of 3 criteria met (nature - Norwell's North River and town-forest conservation land is roughly within a mile of the corridor, though not mapped from this address; NOT quiet on Route 53; no walkable centre). Scored to match the two Norwell records already on file at 399 and 447 Washington Street, which the earlier lifestyle pass also put at 4.

Red flags

It has been listed since 2026-06-01 and was still unlet on 2026-09-10 - about 100 days on a market where the other leads in this slice turn over in weeks. The listing itself supplies the likely reason: the owner is not offering a commission, so agents have no incentive to show it. That is a benign explanation, but a second-floor walk-up at the top of budget with no laundry is another, and the two are not mutually exclusive.

Advantages

800 sq ft is the most space of any 1BR here and clears the 700 floor with room to spare; it is the only apartment in the building with its own private entrance and its own heat and A/C controls, and it has sat on the market since June, which is leverage on rent or on a parking arrangement.

Drawbacks

A second-floor WALK-UP with the flight count not stated, no elevator, and no laundry mentioned in the unit or the building. Parking is 'off street' with no number. $2,100 is exactly the comfortable ceiling and the tenant pays all utilities on top. Norwell is adjacent rather than preferred, about 7 minutes from Route 3.

Suitability 6: per-unit parking count unknown so the base is 5, +1 for in-unit laundry per the manager, +1 because every one of the 24 units is a 2BR, -1 for the laundry contradiction (an aggregator says hook-ups, not machines); no square-footage adjustment because the manager states none. Location 9: Plymouth, preferred town, though Manomet is about 10 minutes from Route 3. Actionability 3: the manager's own vacancies page showed zero results on 2026-09-10 and the Plymouth-specific vacancies link 404s - no published opening, though a 24-unit community turns over and a phone call is exactly how that is found out. Lifestyle 6: 2 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - the Manomet shore and Beaver Dam conservation land; quiet garden-style community per the manager; no walkable centre). | Timeline: actionability 3 to 2 (band CLOSED)

Red flags

The manager's own page and the aggregator listings disagree about the community itself. The manager says 4 three-story buildings with in-unit laundry; an aggregator summary surfaced by search says 2 three-story buildings with washer/dryer HOOK-UPS and rents starting at $2,300. I did not open the aggregator page (forrent.com returned 403, and the newmanpropertiesonline.com unit detail page for 217 Beaver Dam Road #24 returned 404), so neither side is settled. The in-unit vs hook-ups question and the rent are both first-call questions.

Advantages

The only manager-controlled page in this slice, and structurally the best-matched stock in it: 24 units in a preferred town where EVERY unit is a 2BR, with in-unit laundry per the manager and an off-street lot. A community with a real leasing office is also the only lead here that can put the household on a list rather than into a race.

Drawbacks

No rent and no vacancy is published anywhere the manager controls, and the site-wide vacancies page returned zero results on 2026-09-10. Three-story buildings with no stated elevator and no confirmed ground-floor availability puts the profile's access filter at risk. Per-unit parking count unknown. An unopened aggregator figure of about $2,300 would put it over the $2,200 cap.

Affordability 8: $1,900/mo is at the very top of the sub-$1,900 band, $300 under the cap, and the owner pays water. Market-rate: no AMI limit applies, so the household's $43k-$71k band is not tested against a program limit. What does bind is the landlord's own income test (the South Shore norm is ~3x annual rent): 3x $1,900 is $68,400/yr, inside the $71k top of the band but above its middle. Eligibility 8: market-rate, no age rule and no AMI limit; no screening terms are published at all, so this reflects the absence of a barrier rather than confirmed openness. Accessibility 4: unknown - the floor is not stated anywhere on the only page that exists for this unit. Suitability 3: parking is claimed but not counted so the base is 5, -1 for 1BR with no project room, -1 because there is no laundry in the unit or on the site at all, which the profile names a strong preference; no square footage to adjust on. Location 9: Plymouth, preferred town, the downtown waterfront itself, about 5 minutes to Route 3. Actionability 5: no availability date and no contact published - unknown, and unusually hard to resolve, since the only route to the advertiser is the aggregator's own form. Lifestyle 6: 2 of 3 criteria met (nature under 1 mi - the unit overlooks Brewster Gardens; walkable centre, it IS the centre; NOT quiet - this is Plymouth's tourist core).

Red flags

Two problems. First, no contact of any kind is published, which for a downtown waterfront address at a below-market rent is worth caution. Second, source quality: zumper.com is a commercial aggregator equivalent to the Tier-4 list but is absent from the schema allowlist, so it resolves to Tier 3 by default and OVERSTATES this record. Read it as discovery-only.

Advantages

$1,900 is at the top of the affordable band but the owner pays water, and the setting is the best in the slice on paper - a unit overlooking Brewster Gardens, on foot from everything in downtown Plymouth, five minutes from Route 3. Cats allowed, which none of the other Plymouth leads permit.

Drawbacks

No laundry in the unit AND none on site. No contact published at all - no landlord, no manager, no phone - so the only route in is the aggregator's form. No floor, no square footage, no availability date. Parking is claimed but not counted. And Leyden St is the tourist core, which is the opposite of quiet.

Reading the badges

PrimaryAvailability was read on the property's own site, its manager or listing agent, or a state registry, within the last two weeks.
SecondaryRead on a reputable third party (a lottery administrator, a town plan).
Aggregator onlyOnly an apartment-listing aggregator mentions it. Treat as a lead.
ConflictTwo equally good sources disagree, usually on availability. A phone call settles it.
NoFound in a registry but nothing about it could be confirmed yet.
Available nowA unit was listed as open on the day checked.
Waitlist openApplications accepted; wait length usually unknown until you call.
Now ✓A checkmark on the move-in band means a move-in is plausible inside the 3-month window; the band itself (Now, ≤3 mo, 3–12 mo) is how long the wait is.

"~30% of income" means rent is set by the program from household income, so the dollar figure is an estimate for a household of two with income of about $78k, not a listed price. "Min income (2p)" is a floor some fixed-rent buildings require; a household below it does not qualify.

Built from public registries (Housing Navigator MA, MassHousing, HUD, town housing inventories) and each property's own site. Availability changes weekly; the date checked is on every record. Nothing here is an application; every listing links to the place that takes one.
